resources.string: Hands-free control. Everything runs on your phone, offline.
Active — your hand is in control
No supported app in the foreground
Shows whether gesture control is idle, waiting or active.
It has to start here: Android grants the camera only if the service starts while the app is open.
Some required permissions are missing, so the engine cannot run.
Calibrated. Redo it if you change your usual distance or posture.
Not calibrated yet. Default values are in use.
Move your hand up or down: the page follows, like an invisible finger. The further you go, the faster it scrolls.
Move it left or right: volume down or up, progressively.
Closed fist for about two seconds: stop.
Leaving the app also stops it, and closes the camera.
Reads your hand. Images never leave the device and are never stored.
The only way an app can scroll another app. AirScroll does not read screen content.
Draws the small status dot: red off, amber waiting, green active.
Android requires a visible notification while the camera can be used in the background.
Without this, some phones kill the service after a few minutes in the background.
AirScroll turns hand movement into scrolling and volume, so you can use your phone without touching it.
In the kitchen, with a recipe open and your hands covered in flour.
At work, with gloves, tools or dirty hands.
Reading a long PDF or an article.
When touching the screen is difficult or painful.
Gesture recognition runs entirely on your phone.
No internet connection is used or required.
No photo or video is saved anywhere.
The camera stays closed unless a supported app is in the foreground.
The accessibility service does not read the content of your screen, only which app is open.
Four permissions, each with one job.
You can grant them later, but the engine will not start until camera and accessibility are on.
Calibration needs the camera. Grant the permission and come back.
Show your hand to the camera.
Hold the phone the way you normally would and keep your hand in the camera view. It takes about fifteen seconds in total.
Hold your open hand where it feels natural and keep it there. This is how AirScroll learns how far away you usually are.
Try not to move. We measure your natural tremor so that it never turns into unwanted scrolling.
Move your hand up and down a few times, as widely as feels comfortable — not more.
Now move it left and right a few times. This sets the range used for volume.
Your profile is ready. You can always fine-tune it in settings.
Automatic adapts to how big your hand looks, so the same movement scrolls the same amount whether you are close or far.
Hand up scrolls the page up instead of down.
Battery uses a smaller image and the CPU only. Responsive raises the frame rate on capable phones.
Red off, amber waiting, green active.
Turn off the ones you do not want armed. You can add any other app by its package name.
Camera permission is missing: the engine cannot see your hand.

AirScroll needs this service to scroll on your behalf inside other apps. It does not read the content of your screen: it only sees which app is in the foreground, and sends the swipe gestures that your hand movement produces.
Turns hand movement into scrolling, offline.
Open source · Everything runs offline on your phone
Since Android 13, apps installed outside an app store cannot turn on the accessibility service until you unlock it once. If the switch looks greyed out, or you see \"Restricted setting\", do this:
Open the app info with the button below.
Tap the three dots in the top right corner.
Tap \"Allow restricted settings\", then come back here.

Play Protect may also call AirScroll harmful. It flags any sideloaded app that asks for the camera together with the accessibility service — the combination stalkerware uses. AirScroll has no internet permission at all and the code is public, so you can check for yourself. Choose \"Install anyway\" to continue.
